name: Accent
tagline: A macOS assistant that hears what you want to do, finds the right button on screen and highlights it with spoken directions.
problem: Older users struggle with basic interface tasks such as unmuting or turning on captions, the team says.
solution: A menu-bar app captures the request in any language, detects on-screen UI elements with an RF-DETR model, resolves the intent with an LLM and highlights the next element while speaking the instruction.
demo_moment: Team-described: ask in Spanish for a cooking game or ask why nobody can hear you, and the right control lights up.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won “Track: Light The Way” and “Figma Make Challenge” among 307 submissions.
Guides the user to act rather than acting for them, so they learn the interface.
Trained detection turns screenshots into a structured action space.

lessons: Point, don't do: highlighting the next click teaches instead of replacing the user.
